title: Statutory authority and constitutional permission
summary: A court may need both a statute authorizing its action and constitutional permission to exercise that authority. The Constitution can allow a reach that the legislature has chosen not to grant.
notes: Do not assume that identifying a constitutionally permissible outcome answers the statutory question. The source’s historical statutory language may differ from later amendments.

sections.Meaning: A court may need both a statute authorizing its action and constitutional permission to exercise that authority. The Constitution can allow a reach that the legislature has chosen not to grant.
sections.How to work through the question: For personal jurisdiction, read the applicable long-arm provision before applying due process. For subject-matter jurisdiction, distinguish Article III’s outer allowance from the particular statute conferring jurisdiction on the lower federal courts.
